q: What is the youngest age at which you can get a Virginia learner's permit?
exp: Virginia issues a learner's permit at 15 years and 6 months, with no exceptions.
src: dmv.virginia.gov/licenses-ids/learners/apply; Code of Virginia 46.2-335

q: What is the youngest age at which a Virginia teen can get a driver's license?
exp: A Virginia driver's license requires an age of at least 16 years and 3 months.
src: dmv.virginia.gov/licenses-ids/license/applying/eligibility

q: How many of the 10 road sign questions in Part 1 of the Virginia knowledge exam must you answer correctly?
exp: You must answer every sign question in Part 1 correctly before you can move on to Part 2.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 1, Two-Part Knowledge Exam, p. 3; dmv.virginia.gov/licenses-ids/exams/know-exam

q: Part 2 of the Virginia knowledge exam has 30 questions. How many must you answer correctly to pass?
exp: Part 2 has 30 general knowledge questions, and you need at least 24 correct, which is 80 percent.
src: dmv.virginia.gov/licenses-ids/exams/know-exam; VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 1, p. 3

q: You are 16 and fail the Virginia knowledge exam. How long must you wait before taking it again?
exp: Applicants under 18 must wait 15 full days after a failed knowledge exam before retesting.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 1, p. 3; dmv.virginia.gov/licenses-ids/exams/know-exam

q: Which person may supervise a Virginia learner's permit holder from the front passenger seat?
c: Your 20-year-old brother who has only a learner's permit
exp: The supervisor must be a licensed driver 21 or older, or a licensed parent, guardian, brother, sister, half-sibling or stepsibling 18 or older.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-335(A); VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 6, Learner's Permit, p. 31

q: How many hours of supervised driving must a Virginia driver under 18 complete before getting a license?
exp: A parent or guardian must certify at least 45 hours of driving, at least 15 of them after sunset.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-335; dmv.virginia.gov/licenses-ids/learners/ed-reqs

q: How long must a Virginia driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before getting a license?
exp: Drivers under 18 must hold the permit for at least nine months and finish driver education.
src: dmv.virginia.gov/licenses-ids/learners/ed-reqs

q: During which hours may a Virginia driver under 18 not drive, unless an exception applies?
exp: A learner's permit allows no driving from midnight to 4 a.m. A licensed driver under 18 may not drive in those hours except for work, supervised activities, an emergency or with a parent beside them.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-334.01(C) and 46.2-335(D)

q: In the first year of a Virginia license, how many passengers under 21 may a driver under 18 carry, not counting family members?
exp: During the first year, a licensed driver under 18 may carry no more than one passenger under 21, unless they are family or household members.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-334.01(B)

q: On the Virginia knowledge exam, when can you start Part 2?
a: Only after you pass the sign questions in Part 1
b: At any time, in any order
c: Only on a different day from Part 1
d: Only after you pass the vision screening twice
exp: Part 1 must be passed with all 10 sign questions correct before Part 2 begins.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 1, p. 3

q: What must you do after failing the Virginia knowledge exam three times?
a: Wait 90 days, then take the exam again
b: Pass the in-car part of driver education first
c: Pay a $100 fee and retest the next day
d: Finish the driver education classroom part first
exp: After three failures, you must complete the classroom component of driver education, or DMV's 8-hour manual course if you qualify, before testing again.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 1, p. 3; dmv.virginia.gov/licenses-ids/exams/know-exam

q: How often may a Virginia applicant who is 18 or older retake the knowledge exam?
exp: Applicants 18 or older may test once a day; the 15-day wait applies only under 18.
src: dmv.virginia.gov/licenses-ids/exams/know-exam

q: Besides a DMV customer service center, where may many Virginia students take the knowledge exam?
c: At a participating high school, watched by school staff
exp: Through Remote Testing in Schools, students take the DMV exam in a school computer lab with a staff proctor.
src: dmv.virginia.gov/licenses-ids/learners/remote-test

q: What vision must you have to get a Virginia license with no vision restriction?
d: 20/40 or better in one or both eyes
exp: An unrestricted license needs 20/40 or better in one or both eyes and at least 110 degrees of side vision.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 1, Vision Standards, p. 4

q: A Virginia applicant has 20/70 vision in the better eye. What license may this person get, if other standards are met?
a: One restricted to daylight driving only
c: A full license with no restriction
d: A license for interstate driving only
exp: Vision of 20/70 or better with at least 70 degrees of side vision qualifies for a daylight only license.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 1, Vision Standards, p. 4

q: A daylight only license in Virginia lets you drive during which period?
c: From one hour after sunrise to one hour before sunset
d: From half an hour after sunrise to half an hour before sunset
exp: The daylight restriction starts a half hour after sunrise and ends a half hour before sunset.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 1, Vision Standards, p. 4

q: How many passengers under 21 may a Virginia learner's permit holder carry, not counting family members?
exp: A learner's permit allows no more than one passenger under 21, except family or household members or during approved driver education.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-335(C)

q: What is the cell phone rule for a Virginia driver under 18?
b: Calls are allowed at red lights
d: No phone use at all, even hands-free, except in an emergency while parked or stopped
exp: Drivers under 18 may not use a phone while driving, hand-held or hands-free; the only exception is a driver emergency with the car lawfully parked or stopped.
src: dmv.virginia.gov/licenses-ids/learners/restrictions

q: Who certifies a Virginia teen's 45 hours of supervised driving?
a: The DMV examiner, after the road test
b: A parent, guardian or foster parent, on the driver education completion certificate
c: The teen, on a sworn statement
d: Any licensed adult who rode along
exp: A parent, guardian or foster parent signs the driver education certificate to certify the hours.
src: dmv.virginia.gov/licenses-ids/learners/ed-reqs

q: What does the in-car part of Virginia driver education include?
exp: The program has 7 driving and 7 observation sessions of 50 minutes each, plus a final road skills exam.
src: dmv.virginia.gov/licenses-ids/learners/ed-reqs

q: Can a Virginia teen start the classroom part of driver education before getting a learner's permit?
b: No, a permit is required first
exp: Anyone 15 years and 6 months or older may take the classroom portion; a permit is needed only for the driving portion.
src: dmv.virginia.gov/licenses-ids/learners/ed-reqs

q: After finishing driver education, how long does a Virginia teen's Driver Training Certificate (DTS B) work as a license, with a valid permit?
c: 180 days from the eligibility date, or until age 18
exp: The DTS B serves as a temporary license for 180 days from its eligibility date or until the holder turns 18.
src: dmv.virginia.gov/licenses-ids/learners/teen-faq

q: Which court may require a Virginia teen to attend a licensing ceremony?
b: The General District Court traffic division
d: The Juvenile and Domestic Relations District Court
exp: Under 18, you may be required to attend a licensing ceremony at the Juvenile and Domestic Relations District Court where you live.
src: dmv.virginia.gov/licenses-ids/learners/teen-faq

q: After one year with a license, when may a Virginia driver under 18 carry up to three passengers under 21?
c: When driving to or from a school-sponsored activity
exp: After the first year, up to three passengers under 21 are allowed going to or from a school activity, with a licensed driver 21 or older in front, or in an emergency.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-334.01(B)

q: Which trip may a Virginia driver under 18 make between midnight and 4 a.m.?
a: Driving home from a friend's party
b: Driving a friend to the airport
exp: Travel to or from work is one of the exceptions to the midnight to 4 a.m. rule.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-334.01(C)

q: A Virginia driver under 18 is convicted of a first demerit point violation. What does DMV require?
exp: A first conviction under 18 requires a driver improvement clinic, finished within 90 days.
src: dmv.virginia.gov/licenses-ids/improvement/points/under-18

q: What happens after a second demerit point conviction for a Virginia driver under 18?
exp: A second conviction committed under 18 brings a 90-day suspension.
src: dmv.virginia.gov/licenses-ids/improvement/points/under-18

q: What happens after a third demerit point conviction for a Virginia driver under 18?
d: Revocation for one year or until age 18, whichever is longer
exp: A third conviction brings revocation for one year or until age 18, whichever is longer.
src: dmv.virginia.gov/licenses-ids/improvement/points/under-18

q: When do Virginia's passenger and midnight to 4 a.m. limits end for a young driver?
a: One year after the license is issued
d: After two years without a ticket
exp: The under-18 limits expire on the 18th birthday.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-334.01(D)

q: After failing the road skills test at a Virginia DMV office, how long must you wait to retest?
exp: If you fail the road skills test, you must wait two days before taking it again.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 1, Road Skills Test, p. 4

q: Who gives the road skills test to a Virginia driver under 18?
a: A DMV examiner, after a 60-day wait
c: The driver education school, at the end of the in-car course
exp: For applicants under 18, the road skills test is part of the driver education course.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 1, Road Skills Test, p. 4

q: A 25-year-old Virginian who has never been licensed skips driver education. How long must the learner's permit be held before the DMV road skills test?
exp: A first-time adult 21 or older may either hold the permit 60 days or finish driver education.
src: dmv.virginia.gov/licenses-ids/license/applying/eligibility

q: Within how many days of moving to Virginia must a new resident who drives get a Virginia license?
exp: New residents must obtain a Virginia driver's license within 60 days of moving.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 7, New to Virginia, p. 33

q: An adult with a valid driver's license from Germany moves to Virginia. Which test does DMV require after verifying the license?
a: The knowledge exam and road skills test
exp: Holders of licenses from Canada, France, Germany, Japan and South Korea generally need only a vision screening.
src: dmv.virginia.gov/licenses-ids/license/applying/exchange-foreign-dl

q: An adult with a license from a country with no Virginia agreement applies for a license. What must the applicant pass?
b: Vision screening, the two-part knowledge exam and the road skills test
exp: Holders of licenses from non-reciprocal countries take all three tests.
src: dmv.virginia.gov/licenses-ids/license/applying/exchange-foreign-dl

q: What is the Virginia learner's permit fee, paid along with the cost of the license?
exp: The learner's permit fee is $3, plus the yearly cost of the driver's license.
src: DMV 201 fee chart (08/10/2026)

q: What is true of a REAL ID license in Virginia?
a: It is required for every driver
c: It is optional and adds a one-time $10 fee
exp: REAL ID is optional in Virginia and costs $10 once, added to the license fee.
src: DMV 201 fee chart (08/10/2026)

q: What is one limit of a Virginia Driver Privilege Card?
a: It cannot be used to board a domestic flight
b: It does not allow driving after dark
c: It is valid only in Northern Virginia
d: It allows driving only with a supervisor
exp: The Driver Privilege Card is not REAL ID compliant, so it cannot be used to board a flight or enter a secure federal facility.
src: dmv.virginia.gov/dpc

q: An applicant under 18 fills out the Virginia permit application (DL 1P). What else does it need?
b: A parent or legal guardian's signature as consent
c: A notarized letter from the school principal
d: A signed statement from a DMV examiner
exp: Applicants under 18 need written consent from a parent or legal guardian, unless emancipated by court order.
src: dmv.virginia.gov/licenses-ids/learners/apply

q: A red, eight-sided sign with white letters means what?
b: Stop only if traffic is coming
exp: The octagon always means stop, completely, at the line, crosswalk or intersection.
src: core Chapter 2; VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Traffic Signs, pp. 6 to 10

q: A downward pointing triangle with a red border and white center means what?
d: Slow down and let traffic and pedestrians go first
exp: The yield sign means slow, be ready to stop, and let others with the right of way pass.
src: core Chapter 2; VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Traffic Signs, pp. 6 to 10

q: A red circle with a white horizontal bar and the words DO NOT ENTER means what?
a: You may not drive into the road in that direction
b: One-way traffic is coming toward you on your side
d: The road is closed to trucks only
exp: Do Not Enter marks a road you may not enter from where you are.
src: core Chapter 2; VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Traffic Signs, pp. 6 to 10

q: You pass a red rectangular WRONG WAY sign. What should you do?
a: Speed up to clear the road quickly
b: Keep going and use your flashers
c: Slow down, pull over and turn around safely
d: Stop in your lane and wait for help
exp: Wrong Way means you are driving against traffic; get out of the way and turn around with care.
src: core Chapter 2; VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Traffic Signs, pp. 6 to 10

q: A yellow pennant-shaped sign on the left side of the road marks what?
b: A lane that ends on the left
c: The start of a no passing zone
d: A sharp curve to the left
exp: The pennant is the only sign of its shape and marks where passing becomes illegal.
src: core Chapter 2; VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Traffic Signs, pp. 6 to 10

q: A round yellow sign with a black X and two R letters warns of what?
exp: The round yellow sign is the advance warning for a railroad crossing.
src: core Chapter 2; VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Traffic Signs, pp. 6 to 10

q: What does a white X-shaped crossbuck sign at a railroad mean?
a: Trains no longer use these tracks
b: Trains have to stop for cars
c: Treat it like a yield sign and be ready to stop for trains
d: You may cross without looking if no gate is down
exp: A crossbuck marks the crossing itself; look, listen and be ready to stop for a train from either direction.
src: core Chapter 2; VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Traffic Signs, pp. 6 to 10

q: A five-sided sign in fluorescent yellow-green tells you what?
b: You are near a school or a school crossing
exp: The pentagon shape is used only for school zones and school crossings.
src: core Chapter 2; VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Traffic Signs, pp. 6 to 10

q: A yellow diamond sign shows a side lane joining the main lane. Who must make the merge go smoothly?
a: Only the driver already on the main road
b: Only the driver in the joining lane
exp: At a merge sign, two lanes are becoming one and drivers in both lanes share the duty to merge safely.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Warning Signs, p. 8; core Chapter 2

q: A yellow lane reduction sign shows the right lane ending. What should a driver in the right lane do?
a: Merge left when there is space
b: Speed up and pass on the shoulder
c: Stop at the end of the lane
d: Stay right until the lane disappears
exp: The right lane ends soon; its drivers merge left, and drivers on the left let them in.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Warning Signs, p. 8

q: A yellow diamond shows two lanes with a median island between them that ends ahead. What does it mean?
a: A divided highway begins; keep right of the median
b: An exit ramp is ahead on the left side
c: The road widens; you may pass on the right
d: Two-way traffic ahead with no median; keep right
exp: The median ends and the road carries two-way traffic, so keep right.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Warning Signs, p. 8

q: A yellow diamond sign shows a car with wavy skid marks. What should you do when the road is wet?
a: Speed up to get past the wet section
d: Slow down and avoid hard braking or sudden turns
exp: Slippery When Wet means reduce speed, increase following distance and avoid sudden moves.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Warning Signs, p. 8

q: An orange diamond sign with a symbol of a person holding a flag warns of what?
d: A crossing guard at a school
exp: Orange signs mark work zones; this one warns of a flagger who may stop or slow you.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Work Zones, p. 10

q: What does the color orange on a road sign tell you?
a: You are in or near a work zone
exp: Orange marks a work zone and means slow down and stay alert.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Work Zones, p. 10

q: A yellow diamond sign shows a black Y-shaped road symbol. What does it mean?
b: A side road joins from the left
c: The road narrows to one lane
d: The road splits; bear left or right
exp: A Y intersection sign means you must bear either right or left ahead.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Warning Signs, p. 9

q: A yellow diamond sign shows a traffic light. What should you do?
c: Speed up before the light changes
d: Slow down and be ready to stop at the signal ahead
exp: Signal Ahead warns of a traffic signal you may not yet see.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Warning Signs, p. 8

q: A yellow diamond sign shows two arrows, one pointing up and one pointing down. What does it mean?
a: The road ahead carries traffic in both directions
c: Keep right of the island ahead
exp: Two Way Traffic warns that you are leaving a one-way section and will meet oncoming cars.
src: core Chapter 2; VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Traffic Signs, pp. 6 to 10

q: A white sign at a signal reads LEFT TURN YIELD ON, followed by a green circle. What does it mean?
a: Left turns have the right of way on green
b: On a green ball, left turns must yield to oncoming traffic
c: Left turns are banned on green
d: Left turns are allowed only on a green arrow
exp: Traffic turning left on a green light does not have the right of way and must yield to oncoming traffic.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Regulatory Signs, p. 7

q: A white sign shows a U-shaped arrow inside a red circle with a slash. What does it mean?
exp: A red circle and slash forbids the move shown inside it.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Regulatory Signs, p. 7

q: A black and white rectangular sign shows an arrow and the words ONE WAY. What does it mean?
a: Turn only in the direction of the arrow
b: Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow
d: Detour in the direction of the arrow
exp: One Way means all traffic on that road moves in the arrow's direction.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Regulatory Signs, p. 7

q: A yellow sign at a curve shows 30 MPH. What does it mean?
a: The safe speed suggested for the curve under good conditions
b: The new legal speed limit for the road
c: The minimum speed for the curve
d: The speed limit for trucks only
exp: A yellow speed sign is advisory; it is not the legal limit, which still applies.
src: core Chapter 2; VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Warning Signs, p. 8

q: A yellow diamond sign warns of a low shoulder. What does it mean?
a: The road ahead is lower than the shoulder
c: The shoulder is lower than the road surface
d: No shoulder for the next mile
exp: A low shoulder can pull a tire off the pavement; steer back slowly if you drift onto it.
src: core Chapter 2

q: A yellow diamond sign shows a horse-drawn buggy. What does the Virginia manual tell you to do?
a: Slow down and do not use your horn
b: Honk so the driver knows you are behind
d: Flash your high beams before passing
exp: Buggies travel regularly in the area; slow down, do not sound the horn, and pass with at least 3 feet of room.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Warning Signs, p. 8

q: What do blue signs along a highway show?
b: Services such as gas, food and lodging
exp: Blue and white signs give information about motorist services.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Sign Colors, p. 6

q: What do brown signs along a highway show?
exp: Brown and white signs point to historical or cultural interests and recreation.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Sign Colors, p. 6

q: In heavy fog you can make out a sign's outline but not its words. What can still tell you its meaning?
exp: In poor visibility, the shape of a sign may be the only thing you can see, so learn what each shape means.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Traffic Signs, p. 6

q: What does a fluorescent pink sign on the road mean?
b: A traffic incident, such as a crash, is ahead
exp: Pink and black signs warn of incident areas, much as orange signs mark construction.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Sign Colors, p. 6

q: What is the speed limit in a Virginia school crossing zone when no lower number is posted?
exp: Virginia school crossing zones have a 25 mph limit, or a lower posted limit, while the lights flash or during posted times.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-873; Virginia school_zone box

q: What is the most you can be fined for speeding in a Virginia highway work zone when workers are present?
exp: Speeding in a work zone with workers present can cost a fine of up to $500.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-878.1; VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, p. 10

q: What is the fine for holding a phone while driving in a Virginia highway work zone?
d: A warning on the first offense
exp: A handheld device violation in a highway work zone carries a mandatory $250 fine.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-818.2; VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, p. 10

q: A Virginia school zone speed camera can ticket a car going at least how far over the limit?
exp: Photo speed monitoring applies to vehicles going at least 10 mph over the posted limit, with a civil penalty of up to $100.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-882.1

q: When may you turn right on a steady red light in Virginia?
a: After a complete stop, where a sign allows it
b: After a complete stop and yielding, unless a sign forbids it
c: After slowing and yielding, unless a sign forbids it
d: No, Virginia bans right turns on red
exp: Virginia allows a right turn on red after a full stop and yielding, unless No Turn on Red is posted.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Traffic Signals, p. 5

q: When may you turn left on a steady red light in Virginia?
a: Only when both streets are one-way, and only after stopping
b: From any street, after a full stop
c: Only from a two-way street into a one-way street
exp: Left on red is allowed only from one one-way street onto another, after stopping and yielding.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Traffic Signals, p. 5

q: In Virginia, may you turn right on a steady red arrow after stopping?
a: Yes, the same as a red ball
b: Yes, if no pedestrians are present
c: Only if a sign says Right on Red Arrow After Stop
exp: Virginia law prohibits turns at a red arrow unless a sign specifically allows the turn after stopping.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Traffic Signals, p. 5

q: At a Virginia intersection with a green bicycle box painted at the stop line, what is true when the light is red?
b: Right turn on red is allowed after stopping in the box
c: Bicycles must wait behind your car
d: Stop behind the box; no right turn on red
exp: Drivers must stop behind bike boxes, and right turns on red are not allowed at these intersections.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Pavement Markings, p. 13

q: A Virginia police car comes up behind you with siren and flashing lights. What must you do?
a: Pull to the nearest edge and stop until it passes
b: Speed up and pull over when you find a spot
c: Stop right where you are, even in an intersection
d: Pull to the edge, then keep moving slowly
exp: Yield right away: clear any intersection, pull to the edge of the road and stop until it has passed.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-829; VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, p. 16

q: How close may you follow a Virginia emergency vehicle that has its lights flashing?
exp: Never follow an emergency vehicle with flashing lights closer than 500 feet.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Yielding to Vehicles with Flashing Lights, p. 16

q: On an undivided Virginia road, an ambulance with siren and lights comes toward you in the opposite lane. What must you do?
a: Keep going at the same speed
b: Pull over to the edge of the road and stop until it passes
c: Stop in your lane without pulling over
d: Turn onto the next side road
exp: Drivers in the opposite lane of an undivided highway must also pull over and stop.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, p. 16

q: In Virginia, passing a moving emergency vehicle that is sounding its siren with lights on is treated as what?
exp: Overtaking such an emergency vehicle is reckless driving.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-829

q: On a Virginia highway with four lanes, you approach a stopped tow truck with flashing amber lights on the shoulder. What should you do if it is safe?
a: Stay in your lane and keep your speed
b: Move to a lane that is not next to the tow truck
d: Use the shoulder to pass it
exp: The Move Over law tells you to change to a lane not next to the stopped vehicle when reasonable and safe.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-861.1; VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, p. 16

q: Under Virginia's Move Over law, what should you do if you cannot safely change lanes away from a stopped emergency vehicle?
a: Speed up to pass it quickly
c: Sound your horn as you pass
d: Slow down and pass with caution
exp: If changing lanes is unsafe, reduce your speed and proceed with caution.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, p. 16

q: In Virginia, breaking the Move Over law for a stopped vehicle with flashing blue, red or amber lights counts as what?
exp: A violation involving these emergency-lit vehicles is reckless driving.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-861.1(A)

q: Does Virginia's Move Over law also cover a stopped car with its hazard flashers on?
a: No, only police cars are covered
b: Yes; change lanes if you can, or pass with caution
c: No, only tow trucks are covered
exp: Stopped vehicles with hazard lights, caution signs or lit flares are also covered.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-861.1(B); VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, p. 16

q: From which directions must Virginia drivers stop for a school bus that has stopped to load or unload children on an undivided road?
exp: Virginia drivers approaching from any direction must stop and stay stopped until everyone is clear and the bus moves.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-859; VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, p. 15

q: On a Virginia divided highway with a median, a school bus stops on the other side to unload. What must you do?
b: Stop, then go when the driver waves
c: Continue with caution; you need not stop
d: Pull onto the shoulder and wait
exp: Drivers on the far side of a median or barrier need not stop, but should watch for children.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-859; VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, p. 16

q: A Virginia school bus is letting children off but its warning lights are not on. What must you do?
a: Pass slowly since the lights are off
c: Stop only if you are behind the bus
d: Stop anyway until the children are clear and the bus moves
exp: You must also stop if the bus is loading or unloading passengers and the signals are not on.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Stopping for School Buses, p. 15

q: What is passing a stopped school bus while children are getting off in Virginia?
c: A warning on the first offense
d: Legal if you slow to 10 mph
exp: Virginia law classifies failing to stop for a stopped school bus as reckless driving.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-859

q: Where may you make a U-turn in a Virginia city, town or county business district?
a: Anywhere the road is wide enough
c: Only in the middle of a block
d: Only in a parking lot entrance
exp: In cities, towns and business districts, a U-turn is allowed only at an intersection.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-845

q: Virginia law bans a U-turn on a curve or hill where other drivers cannot see your car from how far away?
exp: No U-turn where approaching drivers from any direction cannot see you within 500 feet.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-845

q: A No Left Turn sign is posted at a Virginia intersection. May you make a U-turn there?
a: Yes, if no traffic is coming
d: No; a U-turn counts as two left turns
exp: Virginia treats a U-turn as two left turns, so it is illegal where left turns are banned.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Regulatory Signs, p. 7

q: At 35 mph or less, at least how far before a turn does Virginia law require you to signal?
exp: At speeds of 35 mph or less, signal continuously for at least 50 feet.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-849

q: Above 35 mph, at least how far before a turn does Virginia law require you to signal?
exp: Above 35 mph, signal continuously for at least 100 feet.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-849

q: Under Virginia law, how far before a turn must you signal on a road posted at 35 mph or less?
exp: Virginia law (Va. Code 46.2-849(B)) requires a signal for at least the last 50 feet before a turn at 35 mph or less, and at least the last 100 feet above 35 mph.

q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit on most Virginia roads outside school, business and residential areas?
exp: The default limit is 55 mph for all other roads.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Speed Limits, p. 14; Code of Virginia 46.2-870

q: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit in Virginia school, business and residential areas?
exp: The default limit for school, business and residential areas is 25 mph.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Speed Limits, p. 14

q: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit on an unpaved Virginia road?
exp: Unpaved roads have a default limit of 35 mph.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Speed Limits, p. 14

q: In Virginia, you can be charged with reckless driving for going how fast?
a: 20 mph or more over the limit, or over 85 mph
d: 15 mph over the limit in any zone
exp: Driving 20 mph or more over the limit, or over 85 mph regardless of the limit, can be charged as reckless driving.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Speed Limits, p. 14

q: What is the highest speed limit that may be posted on a Virginia interstate?
exp: Interstates and similar limited access highways may be posted at up to 70 mph.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-870

q: Are radar detectors legal in Virginia passenger cars?
exp: The Virginia manual states that using radar detectors is illegal.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Speed Limits, p. 14

q: On a dry road at 55 mph, what following distance does the Virginia manual recommend?
exp: The manual uses 2 seconds under 35 mph, 3 seconds at 35 to 45 mph and 4 seconds at 46 to 70 mph.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Following Distance, p. 19

q: On a dry road at 30 mph, what following distance does the Virginia manual recommend?
exp: Under 35 mph, the manual's following time is 2 seconds.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Following Distance, p. 19

q: According to the Virginia manual, how should you change your following distance behind a motorcycle?
a: Use the same gap as behind a car
b: Follow closer so the rider sees you
c: Subtract one second because motorcycles stop slowly
d: Add an extra second, and double it in bad weather
exp: Add a second behind a motorcycle and double that distance in bad weather.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Motorcycles, p. 20

q: How are HOV lanes marked on Virginia highways?
a: With a solid yellow line on each side
c: With a white diamond in the center of the lane
exp: HOV lanes carry a diamond-shaped marking; signs give the rider count and hours.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, Pavement Markings, p. 13

q: In Virginia, may a motorcycle with only its rider use an HOV lane?
b: Yes, motorcycles are exempt from the rider count
exp: Motorcycles are exempt from HOV occupancy rules.
src: Code of Virginia 33.2-501

q: What is the fine for a first HOV violation in Northern Virginia (Planning District 8)?
exp: In Planning District 8, fines start at $125 and rise to $250, $500 and $1,000 for repeats within five years.
src: Code of Virginia 33.2-501

q: How close to a fire hydrant may you park in Virginia?
exp: Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Parking, p. 22

q: How close to an intersection may you park in Virginia?
exp: Do not park within 20 feet of an intersection.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Parking, p. 22

q: How close to a railroad crossing may you park in Virginia?
exp: Do not park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Parking, p. 22

q: When you park next to a curb in Virginia, how far from it may your wheels be?
exp: You may not park more than one foot from the curb.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Parking, p. 22

q: In Virginia, how close may you park to fire trucks stopped to answer an alarm?
exp: Do not park within 500 feet of where fire trucks or equipment are stopped answering an alarm.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Parking, p. 22

q: On a Virginia one-way street, on which side may you park?
d: Only the side with a painted curb
exp: On a two-way street park on the right; on a one-way road you may park on either side.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Parking, p. 22

q: In Virginia, how much space must you leave when passing a bicycle?
exp: Virginia law requires passing a bicycle at least 3 feet to its left.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-839; VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, p. 17

q: In Virginia, the lane is too narrow to pass a cyclist with 3 feet of space. What must you do?
a: Change lanes to pass, when it is safe
b: Pass anyway at a slow speed
c: Honk until the cyclist pulls over
exp: If the lane is too narrow for 3 feet of clearance, you must change lanes to pass.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-839

q: When may a Virginia driver drive in a marked bicycle lane?
c: Any time no cyclist is present
exp: Drivers should not use the bike lane except when necessary to turn, and never to pass.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 2, p. 12; Section 3, p. 20

q: When must your headlights be on in Virginia because of the weather?
a: When rain is heavy enough to flood the road
b: When oncoming drivers have turned theirs on
c: On interstates, but not on local roads
d: Whenever your wipers are on because of bad weather
exp: Virginia requires headlights whenever you use your wipers because of bad weather.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-1030; VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Lights, p. 22

q: In Virginia, headlights are required when bad weather keeps you from seeing people or vehicles how far ahead?
exp: Headlights are required when visibility is reduced so that people and vehicles are not clearly seen at 500 feet.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-1030

q: In Virginia, when must you switch to low beams for an oncoming vehicle?
d: Only when it flashes its lights
exp: Dim your headlights within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-1034; VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Night Driving, p. 23

q: In Virginia, when must you use low beams while following another vehicle?
exp: Use low beams within 200 feet of a vehicle traveling ahead of you.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-1034; VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Night Driving, p. 23

q: In Virginia, which crashes must be reported to the police?
b: Only crashes with over $3,000 in damage
c: Crashes with property damage, injury or death
exp: Motor vehicle crashes involving property damage, personal injury or death must be reported to the police.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Traffic Crashes, p. 25

q: You damage an unattended parked car in Virginia and cannot find the owner. What must you do?
a: Wait at the car up to one hour, then leave
b: Leave a note and report the crash to police within 24 hours
c: Report it to DMV within 10 days
exp: Leave your contact details and crash information on a note at the scene and report it to police within 24 hours.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Traffic Crashes, p. 25

q: After a Virginia crash in which no one is hurt and the cars can be driven, what must drivers do?
a: Move the vehicles out of the road right away
b: Leave them in place until police arrive
d: Leave the scene and report later
exp: If the cars can be moved, no one is injured and it is safe, drivers must move them off the road at once.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Traffic Crashes, p. 25

q: Above what amount of property damage do Virginia police send a crash report to DMV?
exp: Officers forward a written report when a crash causes injury, death or total damage over $3,000.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Traffic Crashes, p. 25

q: A Virginia police officer asks you to sign a traffic ticket. What does signing mean?
a: You admit you are guilty of the violation
b: You agree to pay the fine on the spot to the officer
c: You give up your right to a court hearing later
d: You promise to deal with it; it is not admitting guilt
exp: Signing the citation is not an admission of guilt, and refusing to sign can lead to arrest.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Traffic Stops, p. 26

q: A Virginia officer in an unmarked car and no uniform stops you. What may you do?
a: Drive away to the nearest station
b: Ask to see the officer's identification
c: Refuse to roll down your window
d: Get out and walk to the officer's car
exp: If the officer is in an unmarked car or not in uniform, you may ask for identification.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Traffic Stops, p. 26

q: Besides pulling over safely, what does the Virginia manual tell you to turn on when stopped by police?
exp: The manual tells you to turn on your flashers, and your interior light at night.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Traffic Stops, p. 26

q: In Virginia, a driver under 21 with a BAC of at least what level can be convicted of illegally consuming alcohol?
exp: Under 21, a BAC of at least 0.02 but under 0.08 is illegal consumption; 0.08 or more is DUI.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Drunk and Drugged Driving, p. 24

q: Can a Virginia driver be convicted of DUI with a BAC below 0.08 percent?
a: Yes, if the driving is impaired
exp: If your driving is impaired, you can be convicted with a BAC lower than 0.08.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Drunk and Drugged Driving, p. 24

q: What happens the first time a Virginia driver arrested for DUI unreasonably refuses a breath test?
a: A one-year license suspension, as a civil offense
b: Nothing if the DUI charge is dropped
exp: A first refusal is a civil offense with a one-year suspension, on top of any other suspension.
src: Code of Virginia 18.2-268.3

q: What is a second breath test refusal within 10 years in Virginia?
a: A misdemeanor with a three-year loss of license
b: A civil offense with a 90-day suspension
exp: A second breath refusal within 10 years is a Class 1 misdemeanor with a three-year license loss.
src: Code of Virginia 18.2-268.3

q: A Virginia driver is charged with DUI after a breath test shows 0.08 percent. How long is the automatic administrative suspension for a first offense?
exp: A refusal or a BAC of 0.08 or more at the time of the charge brings an automatic 7-day suspension for a first offense.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 5, Administrative License Suspension, p. 30

q: How long does a first DUI conviction cost a Virginia driver's license?
exp: A first DUI conviction brings the loss of the license for one year from the judgment date.
src: Code of Virginia 18.2-271

q: What is the minimum fine for a first DUI conviction in Virginia?
exp: A first DUI is a Class 1 misdemeanor with a minimum fine of $250.
src: Code of Virginia 18.2-270(A)

q: A first-offense Virginia DUI driver had a BAC of 0.17. What mandatory jail time applies?
exp: A BAC of 0.15 to 0.20 adds a mandatory minimum of 5 days; over 0.20 adds 10 days.
src: Code of Virginia 18.2-270(A)

q: In Virginia, what extra penalty applies to a DUI with a passenger 17 or younger in the car?
a: At least 1 more day in jail and a $100 fine
b: At least 5 more days in jail and a $500 to $1,000 fine
c: A 10-hour class and a $250 to $500 fine
d: At least 10 more days in jail and a $2,500 fine
exp: Transporting a juvenile while under the influence adds a mandatory 5 days of confinement and $500 to $1,000.
src: Code of Virginia 18.2-270(D); VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 5, p. 30

q: In Virginia, which set of facts can lead to a charge of drinking while driving?
a: A sealed bottle in the trunk
b: An empty can in the trunk
c: An open container in the passenger area, partly emptied, and signs you have been drinking
d: A sealed six-pack on the back seat
exp: Virginia presumes drinking while driving when a partly emptied open container is in the passenger area and the driver shows signs of drinking.
src: Code of Virginia 18.2-323.1

q: A Virginia driver under 21 is convicted with a BAC of 0.05. What license penalty follows?
exp: Driving after illegally consuming alcohol at 0.02 to under 0.08 brings a one-year suspension plus a $500 minimum fine or 50 hours of community service.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 5, Alcohol Related Violations Under Age 21, p. 30

q: A Virginian under 21 uses a fake ID to try to buy beer. What license penalty applies?
a: A warning letter to your parents
exp: Misrepresenting age brings a fine of at least $500, community service and a 6 to 12 month suspension.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 5, Misrepresentation of Age, p. 31

q: What is the fine for a first offense of holding a phone while driving in Virginia?
exp: A first violation of the handheld device law is a $125 fine; later violations are $250.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-818.2

q: Which phone use is allowed for an adult driver in Virginia while the car is moving?
a: Holding the phone to read a text
c: Typing an address at a green light
d: Using GPS mounted on the dashboard without typing
exp: A device may be used for navigation as long as the driver is not holding it or entering information.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 3, Distracted Driving, p. 24

q: What is the fine for a first offense of live streaming to social media while driving in Virginia?
exp: Live streaming while driving carries a fine of up to $500, with license suspensions for repeat offenses.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-818.3

q: Who must wear a seat belt in Virginia?
d: The driver and every passenger, in front and back seats
exp: The driver and all passengers, front and rear, must be belted; passengers under 18 under the child restraint law.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-1094; VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 4, p. 27

q: What is the penalty for an adult seat belt violation in Virginia?
a: A $25 civil penalty with no points
exp: The seat belt penalty is $25, with no demerit points or court costs.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-1094

q: In Virginia, who is responsible for making sure a 15-year-old passenger wears a seat belt?
c: The passenger's parent, even if not in the car
d: No one; belts are optional under 16
exp: A driver carrying anyone under 18 must make sure that passenger is properly secured, in any seat.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 4, Seat Belts, p. 27

q: Until what age must Virginia children ride in a child safety seat or booster seat?
exp: All children under 8 must be secured in a child safety seat or booster seat.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-1095; VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 4, p. 27

q: Until when must a Virginia child ride rear-facing?
b: Until at least age 2, or the seat maker's forward-facing weight
exp: Forward-facing use is not allowed until the child is at least 2 or reaches the manufacturer's minimum forward-facing weight.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-1095(A)

q: What is the fine for a first violation of Virginia's child restraint law?
exp: A first violation is a $50 civil penalty; a later one can be up to $500.
src: Code of Virginia 46.2-1098; VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 4, p. 27

q: In Virginia, children under what age may not ride in the bed of a pickup truck?
exp: It is illegal to transport children under 16 in a pickup bed, even with a camper shell.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 4, Child Safety Seats, p. 27

q: How often must a Virginia car pass a safety inspection?
exp: Your vehicle must pass an annual safety inspection and display a valid sticker.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 7, Safety Inspections, p. 33

q: What are Virginia's minimum liability insurance limits for injury?
exp: Policies issued or renewed now must cover at least $50,000 per person, $100,000 per crash and $25,000 for property damage.
src: dmv.virginia.gov news, Vehicle Insurance Coverage Requirements Change (SB 1182)

q: After moving within Virginia, how soon must you tell DMV your new address?
exp: Notify DMV of an address change within 30 days.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 7, Address Changes, p. 33

q: How long do demerit points count on a Virginia driving record?
d: Two years from the date of the offense
exp: Demerit points stay valid for two years from the offense date.
src: dmv.virginia.gov/licenses-ids/improvement/points/system

q: A Virginia driver 18 or older gets 18 demerit points in 12 months. What does DMV do?
b: Suspends the license for 90 days and requires a driver improvement clinic
c: Revokes the license for five years
d: Adds a 60-day probation with no clinic
exp: 18 points in 12 months or 24 in 24 months brings a 90-day suspension and a required clinic.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 5, Driver Improvement Program, p. 29

q: How can a Virginia driver earn safe driving points?
a: One for each ticket paid early
b: Five each time you renew on time
c: One per clean calendar year, up to five
d: One for every month with no tickets, with no limit
exp: Safe driving points are earned one per clean calendar year, to a maximum of five; a voluntary clinic also earns five.
src: dmv.virginia.gov/licenses-ids/improvement/points/system

q: A Virginia driver is caught driving without insurance. What must the driver pay to get the license back?
c: Nothing if insurance is bought later
d: A $600 noncompliance fee, plus proof of insurance kept on file
exp: DMV suspends the license until a $600 noncompliance fee is paid and the insurer files a certificate, kept for three years.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 7, Insurance Requirements, p. 35

q: In Virginia, how long must you wait to retake a failed road skills test?
exp: After a failed road skills test you must wait two days before trying again.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 1, Road Skills Test, p. 4

q: What must you do after failing the Virginia road skills test at DMV three times?
a: Wait 90 days, then retest at DMV
b: Pass the in-car part of driver education first
c: Retake and pass the knowledge exam first
d: Pass the classroom part of driver education first
exp: After three DMV failures, you must complete the in-vehicle part of driver education before a fourth try.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 1, Road Skills Test, p. 4

q: An adult 21 or older with no driver education takes the road skills test at Virginia DMV. What form must be brought?
a: The DTS B driver training certificate
b: The DL 7 foreign license form and a translation
c: The CSMA 19 checklist, signed by a licensed driver
d: A notarized letter from a licensed driver
exp: Without a driver education certificate, you need the CSMA 19 checklist certified by a licensed driver who practiced with you.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 1, Road Skills Test, p. 4; dmv.virginia.gov/licenses-ids/exams/road-skills-test

q: Which car can be used for a Virginia road skills test at DMV?
a: One with valid inspection, plates and registration
b: Any car, even without a current inspection
c: A DMV car, which you rent at the test site
d: An autocycle with valid plates and registration
exp: You provide the vehicle, which must have a valid inspection sticker, plates, registration and working safety equipment; autocycles are not allowed.
src: VA Driver's Manual (DMV 39, Apr. 2026), Section 1, Road Skills Test, p. 4
